prompts.title: Recent Form: Rayo vs Elche
prompts.prompt: Create a vertical 9:16 scene, six to ten seconds, for a LaLiga form comparison. Reserve the lower quarter for permanent yellow subtitles. Background GoatLab charcoal #101412. Use warm white #edf0e6 for type, lime #c5ed74 for emphasis, slate #8ca6bf for secondary structure. Layout: top sixth carries a Spanish kicker RACHA RECIENTE and small competition mark; central two-thirds is the comparison stage. Editorial variant first: kinetic typography, no axes or sample claims. Stage 1: team names enter as staggered warm-white slabs from left and right, Rayo Vallecano de Madrid and Elche CF. Stage 2: three rhythmic Spanish words VICTORIAS, EMPATES, DERROTAS pulse in lime and slate sequence, with beat-synced scale pops; a thin lime underline snaps between teams. Stage 3: words stack into a balanced typographic totem, with main emphasis on the middle word EMPATES. Camera: slow vertical push-in with subtle parallax; no invented scores or events. Transition: a lime wipe from center splits to the statistical variant. Exit: type compresses to a slate line that becomes the chart baseline. Statistical variant: grouped count bars on a shared zero baseline, vertical chart in partidos, three clusters VICTORIAS, EMPATES, DERROTAS, two bars per cluster for Rayo Vallecano de Madrid and Elche CF. Common linear scale in partidos, zero baseline, Spanish labels and units; bar values are {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}}, {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}}. Always label sample sizes {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} with Fuente and Muestra from catalog source/sample; if samples are unequal, keep the smaller sample badge visible. Entry: baseline draws left to right, bars grow upward with lime for Rayo and slate for Elche. Main comparison: cluster-by-cluster count bars; emphasis on the largest resolved bar via a warm-white outline, not a new statistic. Camera: shallow top-down tilt to flat chart plane. Transition to exit: bars settle, sample badges remain, lower-quarter subtitles clear, and the chart collapses into GoatLab charcoal. No predictive language.

prompts.title: Goals For and Against
prompts.prompt: Build a vertical 9:16 scene, six to ten seconds, on GoatLab charcoal #101412. Reserve the lower quarter for permanent yellow subtitles. Palette: warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74, slate #8ca6bf. Top sixth: Spanish kicker GOLES and small heading context. Central stage: pitch and data. Editorial variant first: stylized football pitch drawn in slate lines, low opacity, with a single lime ball path. Stage 1: pitch lines draw from center circle outward; team names Rayo Vallecano de Madrid and Elche CF enter as warm-white end-zone labels. Stage 2: an abstract ball travels a curved path from one half to the other, leaving a lime trail; warm-white goal-frame flashes at each end. This is illustrative only, with no invented match event. Stage 3: main emphasis is the tension between attack and defence, shown by the ball path splitting into two arrows, one forward lime, one backward slate. Camera: slow diagonal drift across the pitch with slight parallax. Transition: the ball trail becomes the divider for the statistical variant. Exit: pitch fades, arrows collapse into the chart baseline. Statistical variant: paired horizontal bars, two rows Goles a favor and Goles recibidos, two bars per row for Rayo Vallecano de Madrid and Elche CF. Chart type is paired bar comparison; common linear scale in goles, shared zero baseline; Spanish labels and units, plus Fuente and Muestra source/sample annotation from catalog. Values: Rayo a favor {{home.gf}}, Rayo recibidos {{home.ga}}, Elche a favor {{away.gf}}, Elche recibidos {{away.ga}}; sample badges {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} remain visible. Entry: axis and zero line draw first; bars grow from baseline with lime for Rayo and slate for Elche. Main comparison: attack row against defence row, with no conversion into rates. Emphasis: the larger resolved bar in each row gets a warm-white edge and a soft lime glow. Camera: gentle push toward the paired bars. Transition to exit: bars settle, source/sample badge holds, lower-quarter subtitles remain clear, and the chart dissolves to charcoal. No forecast.

prompts.title: Head-to-Head Historical Counts
prompts.prompt: Create a vertical 9:16 scene, six to ten seconds, with permanent yellow subtitles in the lower quarter. GoatLab charcoal #101412 background; warm white #edf0e6; lime #c5ed74; slate #8ca6bf. Top sixth: Spanish kicker CRUCES and small heading HISTORIAL. Central stage: duel and historical counts. Editorial variant first: present both teams as a visual duel, no axes and no invented match events. Stage 1: two vertical warm-white monoliths enter from left and right, labelled Rayo Vallecano de Madrid and Elche CF; a slate centerline drops between them. Stage 2: lime and slate arcs cross the centerline like a tug-of-war, each arc snapping with rhythmic impact; a neutral warm-white band widens at the midpoint. Stage 3: main emphasis is the duel balance, with the label EMPATES held in the middle and the two team names locked left and right. Camera: slow dolly-in with a slight top-down angle. Transition: the centerline rotates to become the stacked-bar axis. Exit: monoliths dissolve to charcoal as the chart remains. Statistical variant: one horizontal stacked count bar for the complete historical sample, segmented into Rayo Vallecano de Madrid wins {{h2h.homeWins}}, draws {{h2h.draws}}, and Elche CF wins {{h2h.awayWins}}, with total sample {{h2h.total}}. Chart type is a stacked count bar with shared baseline and common linear scale in partidos; Spanish labels, units, and source/sample annotation from catalog with Fuente and Muestra. Entry: bar track draws first, segments extend left to right in warm white, slate, and lime; total badge resolves above. Main comparison: historical win and draw counts within the same sample; no rates and no forecast. Emphasis: the largest resolved segment gets a warm-white edge, while the total sample stays visible. Camera: gentle push toward the stacked bar. Transition to exit: segments settle, source/sample badge holds, lower-quarter subtitles clear, and the bar collapses to a lime line. Historical data is not a forecast.

prompts.title: Recent Form vs Historical Head-to-Head
prompts.prompt: Create a vertical 9:16 scene, six to ten seconds, with permanent yellow subtitles in the lower quarter. GoatLab charcoal #101412; warm white #edf0e6; lime #c5ed74; slate #8ca6bf. Top sixth: Spanish kicker LECTURA and subtitle FORMA RECIENTE CONTRA HISTORIAL. Central stage: two-panel synthesis. Editorial variant first: team reveals and narrative emphasis, no axes and no invented events. Stage 1: Rayo Vallecano de Madrid enters as a lime-edged warm-white card from the left; Elche CF enters as a slate-edged card from the right. Stage 2: a vertical slate divider drops between them; two labels rise, MUESTRA RECIENTE on one side and CRUCES HISTÓRICOS on the other. Stage 3: main emphasis is the tension between the two labels, with lime pulses on the recent side and slate pulses on the historical side; team cards hold as the focal point. Camera: slow lateral reveal with slight parallax. Transition: the divider expands into a two-panel chart frame. Exit: team cards shrink into small chart headers. Statistical variant: two isolated count panels using compatible partido counts, shared count scale in partidos but clearly separate samples. Left panel MUESTRA RECIENTE: Rayo wins {{home.wins}} and Elche wins {{away.wins}}, sample badges {{home.n}} and {{away.n}}. Right panel CRUCES HISTÓRICOS: Rayo wins {{h2h.homeWins}} and Elche wins {{h2h.awayWins}}, total sample {{h2h.total}}. Chart type is paired count bars per panel; Spanish labels and units; source/sample annotation from catalog with Fuente and Muestra. Entry: both baselines draw, then bars extend with lime for Rayo and slate for Elche. Main comparison: recent-sample wins beside historical head-to-head wins; no conversion into rates and no published model estimate is used. Emphasis: the contrast between the two panels, not a single combined total. Camera: steady push-in to the divider, then settle flat. Transition to exit: bars settle, sample badges remain, lower-quarter subtitles clear, and panels fold into charcoal. No forecast.
